gen-dafont-true-north-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono sets its sans letters like pins standing in a wide board, compact and tidy. True North stays stocky and bold above them, so the heading hits hard and the text beneath it stays out of the way.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-julius-sans-one: True North is stocky and bold, its curves refusing to close. Julius Sans One, with hairline monoline strokes and big gaps between letters, gives the pair its lightness against that heavy top.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa reads like glass tubing, hollow and constant in thickness, with a big x-height and stubby ascenders. And across a long stretch of text, that plain sans keeps its curves distinct and wide, never clotting into a grey smear.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-lexend-giga: Tall middles make True North look stocky, and its curves stay stubbornly unclosed. But Lexend Giga is the one built for running text, with flat linework and generous tracking that opens up every word.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega hums softly across a paragraph, drawn with one nib and a visible gap in every c. True North does the loud work up top; the sans just keeps going.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-lexend-tera: Contemporary lines run through both, but they are not alike. Lexend Tera draws like a plotter pen, with crossbars matching the stems, while True North stays stocky and bold above it.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-lexend-zetta: Approachable, first of all, thanks to Lexend Zetta's ribbon-like strokes. True North brings a stocky, tall-middled punch, and the widely tracked sans-serif gives it room to breathe underneath.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-montserrat-alte: Contemporary and round, Montserrat Alternates has a c as open as a bent paperclip. Its strokes show no shading, so a long passage runs smoothly beneath the stocky, bold True North.
gen-dafont-yeasty-flavors-poppins: Poppins brings tall, sturdy lowercase and rope-loose curves that never knot at the ends, with no flicker of thick and thin. Yeasty Flavors, handcrafted and nearly closed, feels like a warm old label next to it.
gen-dm-sans-fs-literata: DM Sans keeps its curve tails held well back from the body, precise and tidy. And Literata, a bookish serif with wide unclosed mouths, can sit a touch larger so its sturdier strokes hold up.
